references.text: Moses' command to remember what Amalek did, and the promise to blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven, repeats and expands on the message from Exodus 17:14.
Balaam's prophecy that Amalek will perish forever confirms God's judgment against Amalek.
God commands Saul to complete the judgment against Amalek by utterly destroying them, fulfilling the promise in Exodus 17:14.
Saul's war against Amalek and the destruction of the people represent a partial fulfillment of God's promise to blot out Amalek.
Samuel reminds Saul that the Lord intended to carry out His wrath on Amalek, referring back to the original judgment.
The Simeonites destroyed the remaining Amalekites at Mount Seir, bringing about the final fulfillment of the judgment against Amalek.
Haman the Agagite, a descendant of Amalek's royal line, shows that hostility toward God's people continued.
The preceding context describes the actual battle against Amalek, which led to God's command to write down the event.
Another example where God commands Moses to write words in a book, illustrating the pattern of preserving God's word in writing.
God commands Moses to write a song and teach it to the Israelites, similar to other commands for written preservation.
Both verses establish Joshua's role as God's chosen warrior and future leader through direct commission from the Lord.
It creates a theological contrast between preserving a reminder of God's provision (manna) and preserving a reminder of God's judgment on enemies.
